The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: tired of having nothing interesting to do.

notes: Used both as a na-adjective (退屈な) to describe something boring and as a noun (退屈) to describe the feeling of boredom.

It differs from 詰まらない (tsumaranai) in that 詰まらない is often used for things that simply lack interest or value, while 退屈 focuses specifically on the restless, stagnant feeling caused by having nothing to do.

senses.definition: The state of being weary or restless because one has nothing interesting or stimulating to do.

examples.text: あまりに退屈で、昼寝をしてしまった。
examples.translation: I was so bored that I took a nap.
examples.emotion: mildly self-deprecating, explaining why they gave up on the afternoon

senses.definition: Describing something that is uninteresting, dull, or monotonous.

examples.text: 退屈な会議がやっと終わった。
examples.emotion: relieved and slightly grumpy, having finally escaped a tedious task
